Q: Intellij IDEA - How to set Airbnb code styling in my project A:

I’m using WebStorm from the IntelliJ IDEA family of IDEs. So I hope your settings are similar.

First, go to Language and Frameworks → JavaScript → Code quality tools → ESLint. Or simply search for ESLint. There you have to add where your ESLint package is. npm install eslint in your project or globally. And add the path from your ESLint install folder in the node_modules folder.

Then you have to add the Airbnb configuration file. npm install eslint-config-airbnb or similar and add the path to the linters/.eslintrc file from the installed folder.

Q: Volatile Variable Coherence A:

Apparently, for processors that support cache coherence, this really doesn't matter, at least in simple scenarios

seq_cststores are a lot slower on x86 that release / relaxed, usually usingxchg`. Slower for the thread doing the store, especially for its memory operations since it's a full barrier. So it overlaps less well with surrounding work. Not faster for other threads seeing the value.

If there isn't any surrounding work, and all threads are just hammering on a single shared variable, then yeah. But that would be terrible, such a trivial program would be better as a single thread, or not existing.

All processors that we run threads across support cache coherency, so memory_order just has to restrict local memory reordering.

On x86, acq/rel costs the same as relaxed, unless compile-time reordering saves anything in the surrounding code. Other ISAs are weakly ordered, and relaxed can be even cheaper, making fewer other memory operations wait for the shared ones that use atomic.

processing data in batches. And this negated all the delays from atomic

Yes, fewer atomic ops and less contention for the same amount of real work is far better than anything else you could do. You don't want contention for shared cache-lines to be how most of your threads spend most of their time; that's really bad and means the CPU cores aren't getting much done.

I use exchange to capture data.

Huh? You can't replace that with volatile, so if that was actually necessary for correctness, you couldn't get it with volatile.
